A.explanation: The resultant force is zero, but the torques do not cancel because both $F$ forces tend to turn the rod the same way about P.

B.explanation: This is the moment $F \times d$ of only one force about P; the second force on the opposite side contributes an equal additional moment.

C.explanation: Each force gives moment $F \times d$ in the same clockwise sense, so total torque is $F \times d + F \times d = 2F \times d$.

D.explanation: The separation between the forces is $2d$, but torque of a couple is one force times separation, $F \times 2d$, not $2F \times 2d$.

walkthrough: Identify the given information: two equal opposite forces of magnitude $F$, with perpendicular distance $d$ from P to each line of action.
State the rule: moment about P $=$ force $\times$ perpendicular distance from P, with sign set by clockwise or anticlockwise sense.
Left force: moment $= F \times d$ clockwise, since an upward force left of P lifts the left end and drops the right end.
Right force: moment $= F \times d$ clockwise, since a downward force right of P also drops the right end.
Add moments acting in the same sense: total torque $= F \times d + F \times d = 2F \times d$.
This combined turning effect is the torque of the couple about P. This is option C.
